items.frank_statement: FRANK C9 requires a typed no-ambient-authority tool/FFI boundary with opaque permits, child-effect closure, current revalidation and typed resource handling.
items.counterhypothesis: Generic ResourceRef values plus adapter-local conventions are adequate; an explicit ownership/borrow lifetime contract is unnecessary.
items.falsifier: A matched generic-ResourceRef implementation provides equivalent safety, replayability, diagnostics and cross-FFI correctness without hidden adapter semantics.
independent_checks: Current-run executable ResourceTable prototype rejected five unsafe lifetime traces while preserving two valid traces.
WebAssembly Component Model independently defines resources as lifetime-bearing abstract types with unique owned handles and temporary borrowed handles.
WebAssembly Component Model concurrency design independently enforces borrow/drop conditions dynamically across async tasks.
adversarial_checks: Naive generic ResourceRef lowering proxy accepted double-drop, drop-while-borrowed, borrow escape, use-after-move and kind confusion.
The prototype does not prove Ubuntu target behavior, compiler ergonomics, static diagnostic quality or concurrency performance.
Ownership does not substitute for capability/effect authorization; collapsing them would violate the external-authority boundary.
items.reason: Independent primary specification plus executable counterexamples support explicit resource-lifetime semantics, but the evidence supports a canonical IR/runtime candidate rather than a mandatory new surface syntax or a completed Ubuntu backend.
items.claycode_action: Keep CapabilityToken/EffectIntent authority semantics unchanged; add ResourceHandle lifetime semantics as OPEN candidate for WP-03/WP-04/WP-07/WP-09 and test in a real evaluator/FFI lowering before promotion.
